atoms.text: When Amelia was a little girl, her mother told her to always keep an eye on the swallows: “Amelia, every time a storm’s a brewin', you bet you’ll have known at least an hour beforehand as long as you don’t lose sight of them swallows”, she would tell her youngest daughter, “We’ve got to make sure our fishing community is safe. Our lighthouse is well perched up on this hill, so it’s our responsibility, ya hear? Just remember: the lower those swallows fly the closer the storm is.” Amelia had quickly learnt to observe how low the swallows would fly. She would spend hours at a time watching the swallows dash across the sky.

atoms.text: One day, Amelia perceived something particularly phenomenal in the sky. A flock of swallows had gathered together and were dancing unusually hectically. While observing the dark cloud formations, she noticed a cold biting breeze: one that was more biting than usual. The swallows flew lower than Amelia had ever seen before. Her legs were already carrying her to her mother while the swallows danced behind her.

atoms.a: What happens after the swallows fly low in this story?
b: Fishermen catch more fish than usual.

atoms.a: What does the swallows’ low flight symbolise?
b: The safety of the fishing community.
